title: 游子吟
author: Meng Jiao

translation: Thread in a kind mother's hand
Becomes the coat on her wandering son
She sews it tight, stitch upon stitch, before he leaves
Fearing his return will be long delayed
Who says the heart of a blade of grass
Can ever repay the sunshine of three springs

annotations.游子: wandering son — a child living far from home
annotations.寸草: an inch-tall blade of grass — the child, small and fragile
annotations.三春晖: the warm sunshine of all three months of spring — a mother's boundless love

appreciation: China's definitive poem about mothers. Meng Jiao builds it on one domestic image — a mother sewing her son's coat the night before he leaves, stitching tighter because tighter stitches last longer on a long road. The final metaphor is devastating: a blade of grass can never repay the spring sun that made it grow.
